Q: cURL error 35: error:1407742E:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert protocol version A:

It appears that the version of cURL you are using doesn't include OpenSSL, so you'll probably want to install or compile one that does. MacPorts is the way I would recommend:

  1. Install MacPorts

Once installed open terminal:

$ sudo port install curl

After installing you should get something similar to:

$ curl -V
curl 7.65.3 (x86_64-apple-darwin17.7.0) libcurl/7.65.3 OpenSSL/1.0.2s zlib/1.2.11 libidn2/2.2.0 libpsl/0.21.0 (+libidn2/2.1.1)
Release-Date: 2019-07-19
Protocols: dict file ftp ftps gopher http https imap imaps pop3 pop3s rtsp smb smbs smtp smtps telnet tftp 
Features: AsynchDNS HTTPS-proxy IDN IPv6 Largefile libz NTLM NTLM_WB PSL SSL TLS-SRP UnixSockets

$ which curl
/opt/local/bin/curl

Q: How to specify multiple "env_files" for a docker compose service? A:

The way I do it is to move your entire docker-compose.yaml to a new file (e.g. docker-compose-main.yaml), then create a new docker-compose.yaml file with the following:

include:
  - path: ./docker-compose-main.yaml
    env_file:
      - .env-credentials

This works with a simple docker compose up with no other parameters. You automatically get the .env file, but this adds in the .env-credentials file at the top level of the docker-compose-main.yaml file. In my case, I made no changes to the original file other than renaming it. Everything imported fine: networks, services, volumes, etc. and I had access to both the .env and the .env-credentials files. This didn't work with some older versions of podman or podman-compose for some coworkers, but it has always worked for me. For reference, it is working for me currently under podman version 5.6 and docker compose 5.1.0.

$ docker --version
podman version 5.6.0
$ docker compose --version
Docker Compose version v5.1.0
